channel.title: FXStreet Forex & Commodities News
channel.description: Real-time Forex News and the latest trading updates. Stay updated on the latest news about currencies and commodities markets.

item.title: Thai Baht: Stabilizes on inflows after export miss – Commerzbank
item.description: Commerzbank’s Thailand section notes May exports rose 10.6% year-on-year, below consensus and sharply slower than April’s 23.1%, with agriculture shipments weak but electronics still resilient. The government forecasts exports to grow 8% in 2026 as front-loading fades.

item.title: Malaysian Ringgit: Policy support tempers downside but caps upside – MUFG
item.description: Lloyd Chan at MUFG notes the Malaysian Ringgit outperformed, rising 0.4% versus the US Dollar (USD) after Bank Negara Malaysia (BNM) reintroduced a 2024-style FX support measure to encourage repatriation and conversion of offshore earnings.

item.title: Dow Jones Industrial Average wins the week by playing defence
item.description: The Dow Jones Industrial Average (DJIA) is closing the week as the last major US index standing, having rallied more than 1% to settle just below 52,000, with the record high near 52,300 still in view. That reads as strength until you ask where the buying is coming from.

item.title: Fed’s Kashkari: “I have one rate hike penciled in for 2026”
item.description: Federal Reserve (Fed) Bank of Minneapolis President Neel Kashkari said during a panel discussion at the Aspen Ideas Festival 2026 in Aspen, Colorado, that he remains concerned about inflation in the service sector, while also noting some signs of improvement in the labor market.

item.title: WTI Oil weakens as Middle East export recovery tempers supply risk concerns
item.description: West Texas Intermediate (WTI) US Oil falls 3.25% on Friday and trades around $69.05 at the time of writing, after hitting its lowest level since late February at $68.48 earlier in the day.

item.title: US President Trump: Iran broke the ceasefire with Hormuz drone strike
item.description: US President Donald Trump posted on Truth Social on Friday that Iran violated the ceasefire after launching drones at ships in the Strait of Hormuz, with one of them hitting the upper deck of a large cargo-carrying ship.

item.title: Euro holds ground against the US Dollar as traders weigh Middle East tensions and Fed outlook
item.description: EUR/USD trades on the front foot on Friday but remains on track for a second straight weekly loss as the fragile situation in the Middle East and hawkish Federal Reserve (Fed) outlook keep the US Dollar's (USD) downside limited.

item.title: British Pound rebounds as US Dollar rally fades, UK politics stabilize
item.description: The Pound Sterling (GBP) gains 0.20% against the Greenback on Friday as the latter recoils after hitting year-to-date (YTD) highs, with money markets pricing in a less hawkish Federal Reserve (Fed), despite policymakers stating they will focus on inflation.

item.title: Australian Dollar recovers as US Dollar eases on profit-taking
item.description: AUD/USD is recovering near 0.6900 on Friday as the US Dollar (USD) weakens with investors taking profits ahead of the end of the semester after a two-week rally in the Greenback. The move helped the Australian Dollar (AUD) recover some intraday ground, although the full picture remains negative.

item.title: China: Spending set to rebound – Standard Chartered
item.description: Standard Chartered economists Hunter Chan and Shuang Ding note that China’s fiscal spending has underperformed so far in 2026, weighing on growth despite stronger-than-expected Q1 data.

item.title: Australia: Labour market rebound masks emerging slack – UOB
item.description: UOB’s Lee Sue Ann highlights that Australia’s unemployment rate dipped to 4.4% in May with a 40.3k employment gain, mainly in part-time jobs, and participation rising to 66.7%.

item.title: Japan: Food and services signal steady inflation – Societe Generale
item.description: Societe Generale economists Reo Sakida and Jin Kenzaki analyze June Tokyo Consumer Price Index (CPI), noting that overall inflation dynamics in Japan changed little from May despite a modest upside surprise in headline and core readings.

item.title: British Pound steadies against Japanese Yen as markets assess UK politics and Japan intervention risks
item.description: GBP/JPY trades in a narrow range on Friday as traders weigh the latest UK political developments against lingering intervention risks from Japanese authorities, with USD/JPY holding above the 161.00 level.

item.title: South Korea: Retail support and FX divergence – BNY
item.description: BNY’s Geoff Yu highlights that South Korean equities have delivered exceptional returns in 2026 while institutional investors remain net sellers, particularly from the Americas.

item.title: Japanese Yen strengthens on BoJ hike expectations and rising intervention risks
item.description: USD/JPY edges lower on Friday and trades around 161.60 at the time of writing after once again failing to sustain a move above the 162.00 mark. The pair is facing profit-taking as investors remain cautious over the risk of intervention by Japanese authorities to support the domestic currency.

item.title: ECB: Another hike before eventual cuts – Commerzbank
item.description: Commerzbank strategists note that despite lower Oil and gas prices, European Central Bank (ECB) officials still signal at least one more rate increase, which the bank forecasts for September.

item.title: Brent: Oversold rebound risk for crude – TD Securities
item.description: Bart Melek at TD Securities argues that Strait of Hormuz disruptions have driven Oil inventories to historically low levels, leaving Brent oversold and vulnerable to a sharp short-covering rebound.

item.title: Japanese Yen: BoJ normalization supports JPY against US Dollar – MUFG
item.description: Lee Hardman at MUFG highlights that the Japanese Yen remains near year-to-date lows versus the US Dollar, with intervention risks limiting further weakness.

item.title: Malaysia: AI boom offsets energy shock risks – HSBC
item.description: HSBC strategists describe Malaysia as relatively resilient to elevated Oil prices thanks to its status as a net energy exporter and beneficiary of the AI (Artificial intelligence) hardware cycle.

item.title: Indonesian Rupiah : IDR recovery versus bond outflows – BNY
item.description: Geoff Yu at BNY identifies Indonesia as one of the clearest cross-asset signals in Emerging Markets (EM) APAC (Asia-Pacific).

item.title: Gold holds gains above $4,000 but eyes a fourth consecutive monthly decline
item.description: Gold (XAU/USD) holds above the $4,000 mark on Friday as the US Dollar (USD) softens following the latest US Personal Consumption Expenditures (PCE) inflation report, which broadly met forecasts and reduced expectations of a near-term Federal Reserve (Fed) interest rate hike.

item.title: Fed: Rate hikes seen unlikely – Commerzbank
item.description: Commerzbank’s Bernd Weidensteiner argues that despite market expectations for further Fed tightening, falling Oil and gasoline prices should lower U.S. inflation and ease pressure for hikes.

item.title: Brent: Hormuz risk premium still fragile – OCBC
item.description: OCBC’s FX strategists Sim Moh Siong and Christopher Wong highlight that Brent Oil has dropped sharply on optimism over the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz after a US–Iran deal, but warn markets may be underpricing security risks.

item.title: New Zealand Dollar stabilizes after US inflation data as RBNZ hold expectations cap upside
item.description: NZD/USD trades around 0.5650 on Friday, up 0.05% at the time of writing, as the New Zealand Dollar (NZD) remains under pressure despite a weaker US Dollar (USD) following the latest US inflation data.

item.title: Swiss Franc strengthens as US Dollar loses momentum following US PCE inflation data
item.description: USD/CHF edges lower on Friday, retracing all the gains recorded this week as the US Dollar (USD) rally loses momentum following the latest US Personal Consumption Expenditures (PCE) data, which broadly came in line with expectations and showed that underlying inflationary pressures remain relatively

item.title: Gold: More pain before recovery – TD Securities
item.description: TD Securities’ Head of Commodity Strategy Bart Melek highlights that Gold recently broke below $4,000/oz as higher US rates and a firmer Dollar weigh on the metal.

item.title: Czech Koruna: Hawkish CNB supports koruna against Dollar pressure – ING
item.description: EMEA FX Strategist Frantisek Taborsky at ING says the Czech National Bank’s (CNB) June minutes confirm it as the most hawkish central bank in the region after its 25bp hike to 3.75%. Markets price another hike as core inflation risks persist.

item.title: Singapore: Broad-based strength with cautious MAS – HSBC
item.description: HSBC strategists highlight Singapore’s strong 1Q26 Gross Domestic Product (GDP) growth, driven by robust electronics exports, construction and services, making it one of ASEAN’s fastest-growing economies. Despite the energy shock, inflation remains contained for now.

item.title: US Dollar: Momentum softens as data cools – MUFG
item.description: MUFG’s Lee Hardman notes the US Dollar is set for a second straight week of gains but has lost upward momentum as softer US GDP and PCE data, plus dovish comments from New York Fed President Williams, reverse recent hawkish repricing.

item.title: Oil: Market optimism faces supply risks – Commerzbank
item.description: Commerzbank’s commodity team, led by Barbara Lambrecht, warns that recent declines in Oil prices may prove temporary as tanker traffic through the Strait of Hormuz is only gradually recovering and US inventories sit well below seasonal norms.
